## Root cause

In `main/main.c`, the NVS-recovery check had an operator-precedence bug:

```c
if (err == ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES || ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND) {
```

The second comparison was missing `err ==`. Since `ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND` is a non-zero constant, the right-hand operand of `||` is always true, so the whole condition is always true. As a result `nvs_flash_erase()` ran on **every boot**, wiping the `stats` namespace before the previous `boot_count` could be read. `load_boot_count()` therefore always hit `ESP_ERR_NVS_NOT_FOUND`, printing `boot_count=1` (then freshly saving 1) forever.

I confirmed this by dumping the NVS partition (it contained `boot_count: 1` at `0x9000`) and by observing the `no boot count stored yet` log on every reset despite successful commits.

## Fix

Changed the condition to compare both errors:

```c
if (err == ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES || err == ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND) {
```

Now the partition is only erased when NVS actually reports one of those two errors. Log format is unchanged.

## Verification on the board

After rebuilding/flashing, three consecutive resets produced:

```
boot_count=2  (reset reason 11)   saved boot_count=2
boot_count=3  (reset reason 11)   saved boot_count=3
boot_count=4  (reset reason 11)   saved boot_count=4
```

The counter now persists and increments by one per reset.
